content: A communication disorder is a medical condition or disease that impairs or completely prevents the ability to communicate effectively. This impairment can occur in the production, reception, or comprehension of communication. Examples of communication disorders include: Autism: A developmental condition that affects the ability to understand and engage in emotional communication. Aphasia: A condition characterized by the loss of the ability to produce or comprehend language. Learning Disability: A condition that impacts both the speaking and listening components of communication. Dysnomia: A deficit involving difficulty in retrieving words. Asperger Syndrome: A condition that primarily affects social and pragmatic aspects of language. Semantic Pragmatic Disorder: A condition involving challenges with the semantic (meaning-related) and pragmatic (contextual use) aspects of language. Blindness: A defect in the eye or visual system that impacts visual communication. Deafness: A defect in the ear or auditory system that affects auditory communication. Dyslexia: A condition involving a defect in the systems used for reading. Dyscalculia: A condition involving a defect in the systems used for communicating numerical information. Expressive Language Disorder: A condition that affects speaking and understanding, despite no delay in non-verbal intelligence. Mixed Receptive-Expressive Language Disorder: A condition that impacts speaking, understanding, reading, and writing, while non-verbal intelligence remains unaffected.
